wifi.description: Wi-Fi network for charger {name}: 2.4 GHz, WPA2 security. 5 GHz networks, WPA3 and mixed modes (WPA/WPA2, WPA2/WPA3) will not work. The name and password may contain only Latin letters without accents, digits and symbols.

data.host: Home Assistant address in your network
data.plug_and_charge_off: Start charging by command, not by plugging in

data_description.host: The IP address of the computer or server running Home Assistant in your home network, for example 192.168.1.10. If a different address is shown here, delete it and enter yours.
data_description.plug_and_charge_off: Recommended. Charging starts by a command from Home Assistant or by the schedule, not as soon as the cable is plugged in.

passport.title: Charger version
passport.description: Charger {serial} received the Wi-Fi settings. Check that your charger version is selected — the number of phases and the power, as on the charger's rating plate. If a different one is selected, select yours.

enable_ocpp.title: Switch OCPP on at the charger
enable_ocpp.description:
1. Wait for the Wi-Fi icon on the charger screen.
2. On the charger press OK, choose Wi-Fi, switch OCPP on and leave the menu.
3. Click Submit.

If the Wi-Fi icon does not appear, close this window, check the network name and password and start again.

not_connected.title: The charger has not connected yet

manual_address.title: Server address for the charger
manual_address.description:
Check that the address below contains the IP address of your Home Assistant. If it shows a different address, for example ws://172.17.0.2, close this window, open Settings → System → Network, in Local network switch Automatic off, enter http://computer-IP-address:8123, click Save and start again.

In the EV-Charger app, in the OCPP settings, enter:

- server address: `{url}`
- ChargeID: `{serial}`

Then on the charger press OK, choose Wi-Fi — the address you entered is shown there — switch OCPP on and leave the menu. Click Submit.

discovery_confirm.title: Charger {serial} connected
discovery_confirm.description: Charger {serial} connected to Home Assistant. Choose its version to add it.

progress.provision: Writing the settings to the charger — about half a minute.
progress.wait_connect: Waiting for the charger to connect — up to 10 minutes.

error.no_devices: Charger not found. Switch OCPP off on the charger, close the app on your phone, move the Bluetooth adapter closer to the charger and click Submit.
error.ssid_ascii: The charger accepts only Latin letters, digits and symbols in the network name. Rename the network in the router settings.
error.ssid_long: The network name is longer than 32 characters. Rename the network in the router settings.
error.password_ascii: The charger accepts only Latin letters, digits and symbols in the password. Change the password in the router settings.
error.password_long: The password is longer than 32 characters. Change the password in the router settings.
error.host_ascii: Enter an IP address, for example 192.168.1.10.
error.host_empty: Enter the address of Home Assistant.
error.port_busy: This port is used by another program. Enter another one, for example 9001.
error.serial_invalid: The serial number consists of 12 digits.
error.ble_not_found: Charger not found. Switch OCPP off on the charger, close the app on your phone, move the Bluetooth adapter closer to the charger and click Submit.
error.ble_connect_failed: Could not connect to the charger. Switch OCPP off on the charger, close the app on your phone and click Submit.

error.ble_rejected: The charger did not accept the settings. Click Submit again.

abort.already_in_progress: This charger is already being set up in another window. Close this window. If there is a card of this charger in Discovered, continue from it.

abort.ble_not_charger: This is not a GNLT charger.

init.title: Charger settings

data.auto_start: Start when the cable is connected
data.resume_after_power_loss: Continue charging after a power cut
data.meter_interval: How often the charger sends readings, seconds

data_description.auto_start: Home Assistant starts the charge itself when you plug the cable into the car. Cannot be combined with the schedule: turning one on turns the other off.
data_description.resume_after_power_loss: If the power goes off during charging, Home Assistant resumes charging when the power comes back, if the cable was not unplugged. Works with charger firmware 2.8 and newer.
data_description.price: Price per 1 kWh. 0 — the cost is not calculated.
data_description.night_price: For a two-zone tariff. 0 means a single tariff. Energy delivered at night is priced at this rate even if the charge started in the day.

init.description: Prices are per 1 kWh, in the currency of Home Assistant ({currency}).

state.evcommunicationerror: Charger and car did not agree

charging_without_session.name: Charging started by the charger itself

empty_session.name: The car did not start charging

schedule_stop_at_end.name: Stop at the end of the schedule

not_connected.message: The charger is not connected to Home Assistant.

no_answer.message: The charger did not answer in time. Try again.

replug.message: The car did not take current last time, and the charger will not accept a new start. Unplug the cable, plug it in again and start.
